svg.title: Post-Tyler Certificate Control Structure
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-post-tyler-certificate-control; chapter number: 11; title: Post-Tyler Certificate Control Structure; subtitle: Who guards a certificate after Tyler v. Hennepin; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Certificate Holder; headcount: Solo holder backed by tax sale counsel; focus: Protect each certificate from notice defects, bankruptcy stays, equity claims and unconfirmed redemptions.; spokes: role: Tax Sale Counsel; type: Outside legal; kpi: Confirms how the county issues deeds; mandamus or judicial foreclosure plus suing the county as the fallback.; role: Court File and Records Review; type: Diligence; kpi: Court file and county records pulled on every certificate; ready for the court form's question on equity in the property.; role: Notice Auditor; type: Compliance; kpi: Every interest holder noticed, including trustees, with additional reasonable steps documented after certified mail comes back.; role: Bankruptcy and Redemption Monitor; type: Operations; kpi: Bankruptcy checked up to the minute of sale (a 9:48 a.m. filing voids a 10:00 a.m. auction); ticklers at two and three weeks after a redemption closing until proof arrives.; caption: After the 9-0 Tyler ruling, a certificate is only as safe as its notice trail, its bankruptcy check and written proof of redemption.; assumptions note: Roles are functions, not required hires. Practitioners split sharply: Lynette Lowitz would not buy certificates now, while Tax Sale Secrets frames the worst case as a few months of delay.; note: Sources: Tax Sale Resources (d67aVfAEUxg @ 00:25:05); The Devine Law Group (qAoyeFTuxms @ 00:15:05, 00:16:45); Florida Trust, Real Estate, Probate, & Foreclosure (RlQwxNYiqok @ 00:15:33); Behind The Servicing (au90-c2Pwvo @ 00:00:17); The Deed | Real Estate (sb6T0Xe5siY @ 00:06:20).
